newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Record gas oil volume traded.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Record gas oil volume traded.

text.p: The strength in Singapore gas oil prices due to sustained frenzied buying by a Singapore trader was further boosted by a rally in crude and gas oil prices in the London's futures market, traders said on Friday.

The trader and its sister company, together with a Japanese trader shattered their own single-day record by buying nearly 1.9 million barrels in 12 cargoes, up from Tuesday's purchases of 1.35 million barrels.
The local traders have to date bought at least 13 million barrels since they started their buying binge on March 3.
"This is unhealthy," one trader said. "When is this going to end, when the industry stops and has to sell to one party?"
But most traders believe that the buying binge has still not yet ended.
The 12 cargoes, for end April were traded between $26.95 and $27.20 per barrel, while early May cargoes were done at $26.70-$26.80, marginally higher than the deals done on Thursday.
Traders noted that the ongoing tension between Iran and Europe over the killing of Kurdish exiles has perked up Brent crude futures by 22 cents to $18.16 while gas oil futures gained $3.50 per tonne.
This provided the underlying fundamental support to the sustained strength of gas oil values in Singapore made possible by the buying spree.
Jet fuel was traded at $24.70 for 120,000 barrels lifting May 3-7, edging up from recent low levels.
